note.question: Can a firm use demographic or horizon diversity and asymmetric performance pay to preserve peer-enforced effort without making employee collusion too attractive?
note.overview: A principal designs a short-term performance contract for two agents who interact forever. The agents use repeated-game punishments to sustain productive cooperation but can also use a correlation device and implicit side arrangements to sustain collusive effort patterns. The paper explicitly requires a Pareto-undominated subgame-perfect team equilibrium and designs wages and team composition to deter regret-free collusion.

components.label: Pareto-undominated subgame-perfect team equilibrium with collusion-proof contracting
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Pareto-undominated subgame-perfect team equilibrium with collusion-proof contracting. The intended work-work path must be sustainable as a subgame-perfect equilibrium through mutual-monitoring punishments. The additional Pareto constraint eliminates any other subgame-perfect, possibly correlation-device-supported equilibrium that both agents would prefer without subsequent regret. The principal minimizes wages subject to both requirements, so the selected team equilibrium is cooperative and collusion proof.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At the outset, the principal permanently selects two agents and commits to short-term wages contingent only on the current task outcome. In every period, both agents privately choose work or shirk, observe each other's effort, and receive success-contingent wages if the stochastic team task succeeds. Their actions and continuation play can follow history-dependent punishments; a correlation device may coordinate collusive alternating-effort profiles. The same strategic interaction repeats over an infinite horizon.
